mainTopic: Which animals may be used to redeem a פטר חמור: the שה/פסח comparison, a בן פקועה, a נדמה, and פסולי המוקדשין.
overview: The משנה lists animals that may not be used to redeem a פטר חמור, such as a calf, a wild animal, a טריפה, a כלאים and a כוי. רבי אליעזר permits a כלאים. The גמרא explains that the list follows בן בג בג, who links the word שה here to the word שה by the קרבן פסח. The doubled word תפדה then allows female, blemished and older lambs. Next the גמרא asks about a בן פקועה: מר זוטרא forbids it because of the פסח comparison, and רב אשי permits it. It then asks about a נדמה, a sheep that looks like a goat, according to the רבנן. Two proofs are brought from ברייתות, and both are pushed aside. Finally it asks about redeeming with פסולי המוקדשין, and רב מרי rules from 'כצבי וכאיל' that you may not. The amud ends as the גמרא begins to draw a new point from his answer, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Animals that cannot redeem a firstborn donkey
steps.stepSummary: The משנה lists six kinds of animals that may not be used to redeem a פטר חמור.
steps.simpleTranslation: MISHNA: You may not redeem a firstborn donkey with a calf, a wild animal, a slaughtered animal, a טריפה, a כלאים, or a כוי.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה opens with a list of animals that may not be used to redeem a פטר חמור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה says a פטר חמור is redeemed with a שה, which means a sheep or a goat. This list rules out animals that are not a שה at all (a calf, a wild animal), animals that are not alive and healthy (slaughtered, טריפה), and animals whose status is mixed or doubtful (כלאים, כוי).

keyTerms.meaning: We redeem, here meaning freeing the firstborn donkey from its holiness by giving a lamb in exchange
A firstborn male donkey, which must be redeemed with a lamb
An animal with a fatal defect
A hybrid; here, a cross between a sheep and a goat
An animal that might be domestic or might be wild; its status is doubtful

phrases.english: MISHNA: One may not redeem
phrases.notes: The thing being redeemed is the firstborn donkey from the previous משנה. The rest of the list tells us what you can't use to redeem it.

phrases.english: neither with a calf nor with a wild animal,
nor with a slaughtered animal nor with a tereifa,
nor with a hybrid nor with a koy.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵין פּוֹדִין לֹא בְּעֵגֶל וְלֹא בְּחַיָּה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A פטר חמור may not be redeemed with a calf, a wild animal, a slaughtered animal, a טריפה, a כלאים, or a כוי.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר permits a כלאים but not a כוי
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר allows redemption with a כלאים, because it counts as a שה, but forbids a כוי, because its status is doubtful.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר permits a sheep-goat hybrid, because it is still a שה, but forbids a כוי, because it is a doubtful case.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אליעזר disagrees with part of the list and permits using a כלאים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since a sheep and a goat are both called שה, a cross between them is still a שה in רבי אליעזר's view, so it works for redemption. A כוי is different: it may not be a domestic animal at all, so we cannot be sure it is a שה.

keyTerms.meaning: Permits
Forbids
A lamb or kid; the general word for sheep and goats
A doubt; a case of uncertain status

phrases.english: And Rabbi Eliezer permits [redeeming] with a hybrid
because it is a seh (lamb),
but forbids [redeeming] with a koy
because it is a doubt.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A dissenting opinion on one item (כלאים) in the list from step 1, while agreeing about כוי.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי אליעזר, a כלאים may be used because it is a שה; a כוי may not, because it is a ספק.

steps.title: A כהן must set aside a שה before keeping the donkey
steps.stepSummary: If an unredeemed פטר חמור was given to a כהן, he may not keep it until he sets aside a שה in its place.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he gave the firstborn donkey to a כהן, the כהן may not keep it until he designates a שה in its place.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה adds a new rule: even the כהן who receives the donkey has to redeem it with a שה before he may keep it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Handing the donkey to the כהן does not take away its holiness. Someone still has to redeem it with a שה, so the כהן does it himself before he uses the donkey.

keyTerms.meaning: Permitted
To keep it (for his own use)
That he sets aside or designates
In its place

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה has three parts: the list of animals that may not be used, רבי אליעזר's view on כלאים and כוי, and the rule that a כהן must redeem the donkey himself before keeping it.

phrases.english: If he gave it to a priest,
the priest is not permitted to keep it
until he designates a lamb in its place.

steps.triggerLanguage: נְתָנוֹ לְכֹהֵן אֵין הַכֹּהֵן רַשַּׁאי לְקַיְּימוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new, separate ruling in the same משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A כהן who receives an unredeemed פטר חמור must set aside a שה in its place before keeping it.

steps.title: Whose opinion is the משנה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which תנא is the author of the first part of the משנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: GEMARA: Whose view is our משנה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens by asking who holds the view in the משנה's list. This sets up the next step, which gives the answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה rules out many animals without giving a source. The גמרא wants to know which תנא holds this and how he learns it from the פסוקים.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה
Who is it? (Whose opinion?)

phrases.english: GEMARA: Whose [opinion] is our mishna?

steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא holds that all the listed animals are not valid for redeeming a פטר חמור.

steps.title: בן בג בג compares שה here to שה by the פסח
steps.stepSummary: The משנה follows בן בג בג, who uses a גזירה שוה on the word שה to exclude all the listed animals, just as they are excluded from the קרבן פסח.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is בן בג בג. A ברייתא teaches that בן בג בג says: The תורה says שה here (by the firstborn donkey) and שה there (by the קרבן פסח). Just as there all these kinds are excluded, so too here all these kinds are excluded.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the משנה follows בן בג בג, and quotes his ברייתא to show where he learns it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same word שה appears in both places, so whatever the word excludes by the פסח it also excludes by the firstborn donkey. Calves, wild animals, slaughtered animals, טריפות, כלאים and כוי are not valid for a פסח, so they are not valid for redemption either.

keyTerms.meaning: A תנא whose opinion the משנה follows
As it is taught in a ברייתא
It says here... and it says there; the opening of a גזירה שוה
Excluding
Literally 'these names'; all the kinds of animals listed

steps.whyThisMatters: This גזירה שוה is the base of the whole סוגיא. The next steps test how far the comparison to the פסח really goes.

phrases.english: It is ben Bag Bag,
as it is taught: Ben Bag Bag says:
It is stated here "lamb,"
phrases.notes: Here means the firstborn donkey: "redeem with a שה" (שמות יג:יג).

phrases.english: and it is stated there "lamb,"
phrases.notes: There means the קרבן פסח: "each man shall take a שה" (שמות יב:ג).

phrases.aramaic: מָה לְּהַלָּן פְּרָט לְכׇל הַשֵּׁמוֹת הַלָּלוּ,
phrases.english: just as there it excludes all these names,

phrases.aramaic: אַף כָּאן פְּרָט לְכׇל הַשֵּׁמוֹת הַלָּלוּ.
phrases.english: so too here it excludes all these names.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 4.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The משנה follows בן בג בג, who learns from a גזירה שוה of שה/שה with the קרבן פסח that all the listed animals are excluded.

steps.title: Should the lamb also be male, unblemished and one year old?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: if we copy the פסח, the redemption lamb should also have to be male, unblemished, and in its first year.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if so, just as there (the פסח) the lamb must be male, unblemished, and in its first year, so too here it should have to be male, unblemished, and in its first year?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes the comparison further and asks whether all the פסח's requirements should apply to the redemption lamb.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the גזירה שוה makes the firstborn donkey's lamb follow the פסח's lamb, it seems all the פסח's rules should carry over. That would require a male, unblemished lamb within its first year, which is a much stricter rule.

keyTerms.meaning: If so, just as...; it opens a challenge that stretches the comparison
Male
Unblemished
In its first year

phrases.english: If so, just as there
phrases.notes: There means the קרבן פסח again, which שמות יב:ה says must be a male, unblemished, in its first year.

phrases.english: [it must be] male, unblemished, and in its first year,

phrases.aramaic: אַף כָּאן זָכָר תָּמִים וּבֶן שָׁנָה?
phrases.english: so too here, male, unblemished, and in its first year?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי מָה לְהַלָּן זָכָר תָּמִים וּבֶן שָׁנָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges how far the גזירה שוה from step 5 goes.
steps.kashyaTarget: בן בג בג's גזירה שוה of שה/שה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the comparison carries over the פסח's exclusions, it should also carry over the פסח's requirements (male, unblemished, first year).

steps.title: The doubled 'you shall redeem' includes those lambs
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the תורה repeats תפדה, and this repetition includes females, blemished lambs, and older lambs.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse says תפדה and again תפדה, which comes to include more.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by pointing to the repeated word תפדה, which widens which lambs may be used.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word תפדה appears twice about the firstborn donkey (שמות יג:יג and שמות לד:כ). The extra word is read as a ריבוי that includes lambs the פסח would not allow: female, blemished, or older than a year.

keyTerms.meaning: The verse says; it introduces a source from a פסוק
You shall redeem
It included; the extra word widens the law

phrases.english: The verse states:
"You shall redeem," "you shall redeem": it included.
phrases.notes: The word shows up twice, in שמות יג:יג and שמות לד:כ. The extra one adds female, blemished and older lambs.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 6.
steps.terutzResolutionType: A separate ריבוי from a repeated word limits how far the גזירה שוה reaches.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: All of the פסח's requirements should apply to the redemption lamb.
steps.terutzMaskana: The doubled תפדה includes female, blemished, and older lambs, so those פסח requirements do not apply.

steps.title: Then include all the excluded animals too?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: if the doubled תפדה includes more, why not include all the animals the משנה excluded?
steps.simpleTranslation: If the doubled תפדה includes, then it should include all these animals (the ones in the משנה) as well?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns the answer around: if the ריבוי widens the law, why does it stop at female or blemished lambs and not include everything?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once we have a ריבוי, there seems to be no clear line. It might include calves, wild animals, כלאים and the rest, which would cancel the משנה's list.

keyTerms.meaning: Even
All these
Also, too

phrases.english: If "you shall redeem," "you shall redeem" includes,
then even all these as well?
phrases.notes: All these means the animals the משנה excluded: calf, wild animal, slaughtered, טריפה, כלאים, כוי.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי ״תִּפְדֶּה״ ״תִּפְדֶּה״ רִיבָּה, אֲפִילּוּ כֹּל הָנֵי נָמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the תירוץ of step 7 by asking how far its ריבוי goes.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ריבוי of the doubled תפדה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ריבוי with no stated limit should include even the animals the משנה excluded.

steps.title: Otherwise the word 'lamb' would have no purpose
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers: if the ריבוי included everything, the גזירה שוה from שה would accomplish nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, what would the comparison of שה and שה accomplish?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a rhetorical question: the ריבוי can't include everything, or the word שה would be pointless.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both sources must have some job. The ריבוי of תפדה includes lambs that fail the פסח requirements (female, blemished, or older than a year), while the גזירה שוה of שה still excludes the animals listed in the משנה. If the ריבוי covered everything, the word שה would do nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: If so
What does it accomplish for him?

steps.confusionAlert: This line is phrased as a question, but it is the גמרא's answer. It shows that the ריבוי must have a limit, because the word שה has to teach something.
steps.whatToRemember: The two sources split the work. The גזירה שוה of שה/שה excludes animals that are not a proper שה (calf, wild animal, slaughtered, טריפה, כלאים, כוי). The doubled תפדה includes female, blemished, and older lambs.

phrases.english: If so,
what does "lamb," "lamb" accomplish for him?
phrases.notes: For him means for בן בג בג: his comparison of the two times שה appears would teach nothing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 8.
steps.terutzResolutionType: The word must have a purpose: the ריבוי cannot make the גזירה שוה meaningless.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The doubled תפדה includes every animal, even those the משנה excluded.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ריבוי includes only what the גזירה שוה does not exclude; the listed animals stay excluded by שה/שה.

steps.title: New question: redeeming with a בן פקועה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether a בן פקועה may be used to redeem a firstborn donkey. It narrows the question to the opinion of the רבנן, since according to רבי מאיר it is clearly a full lamb.
steps.simpleTranslation: They asked: may you redeem a firstborn donkey with a בן פקועה? According to רבי מאיר there is no question. He says a בן פקועה needs its own שחיטה, so it is a full lamb. The question is only according to the רבנן, who say its mother's שחיטה already makes it permitted to eat.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a brand-new question about which lamb may be used for פדיון פטר חמור. It first narrows down whose opinion the question really applies to.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A בן פקועה is a live fetus found inside an animal after the mother was slaughtered. For רבי מאיר it needs its own שחיטה, which shows it is a normal living animal, so it obviously counts as a שה. For the רבנן, the mother's שחיטה already covers it, so it is treated like meat that has already been slaughtered. That is what makes the question real.

keyTerms.meaning: A question was raised before them (the start of a real doubt)
A live fetus taken from its mother after she was slaughtered
Needs its own ritual slaughter
Its mother's slaughter makes it permitted to eat
A proper, full-fledged lamb

steps.confusionAlert: The question is not whether a בן פקועה may be eaten. Everyone agrees it may be. The question is whether it counts as a living שה for redeeming a donkey.

phrases.english: A question was raised before them:
What is the law about redeeming with a בן פקועה?

phrases.aramaic: אַלִּיבָּא דְּרַבִּי מֵאִיר לָא תִּיבְּעֵי לָךְ,
phrases.english: According to רבי מאיר, you should not ask this,
because since רבי מאיר said:
A בן פקועה requires its own slaughter,
it is a full-fledged lamb.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא כִּי תִּבְּעֵי לָךְ אַלִּיבָּא דְּרַבָּנַן,
phrases.english: Rather, when you ask, ask according to the רבנן,
who say: the slaughter of its mother makes it permitted.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיבַּעְיָא לְהוּ: מַהוּ לִפְדּוֹת בְּבֶן פְּקוּעָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new question about which animals qualify as a שה for redemption.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a בן פקועה, according to the רבנן, counts as a שה for redeeming a firstborn donkey.

steps.title: The two sides of the doubt
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא spells out both sides. Is a בן פקועה like slaughtered meat in a basket, or is it a lamb because it is running around alive?
steps.simpleTranslation: Is it like meat sitting in a basket? Or maybe, since right now it is running around, we call it a שה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא lays out the two possible ways to see a בן פקועה according to the רבנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Side one: legally it is already 'slaughtered' through its mother, so it is like ready meat, and you cannot redeem with a slaughtered animal. Side two: in reality it is alive and walking, so it looks and acts like a שה. The doubt is between its legal status and its physical reality.

keyTerms.meaning: Like meat in a basket, meaning already-slaughtered meat
Or perhaps (introduces the other side)
Runs and goes around, meaning it is alive and moving

phrases.english: Is it like meat sitting in a basket,
phrases.notes: The idea is that it already counts as slaughtered meat, just waiting to be eaten.

phrases.english: or perhaps:
since right now, at least, it runs around,
we call it a "lamb"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reasoning behind the question raised in step 10.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether legal 'slaughtered' status or physical aliveness decides if a בן פקועה is a שה.

steps.title: מר זוטרא and רב אשי disagree
steps.stepSummary: מר זוטרא says you may not redeem with a בן פקועה. רב אשי says you may.
steps.simpleTranslation: מר זוטרא said: we do not redeem with it. רב אשי said: we do redeem with it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings two אמוראים who answer the question in opposite ways.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מר זוטרא takes the first side: it is like slaughtered meat, so it cannot be used. רב אשי takes the second side: it is alive, so it counts as a שה. The next step shows what drives מר זוטרא's view.

keyTerms.meaning: We do not redeem (with it)
We do redeem (with it)
An אמורא who holds you may not redeem with a בן פקועה

phrases.english: מר זוטרא said: we do not redeem with it,
and רב אשי said: we do redeem with it.

steps.triggerLanguage: מָר זוּטְרָא אָמַר: אֵין פּוֹדִין, וְרַב אָשֵׁי אָמַר: פּוֹדִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives two opposite answers to the question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A dispute: מר זוטרא says no, רב אשי says yes.

steps.title: רב אשי challenges the comparison to פסח
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי guesses that מר זוטרא learns the rules from the קרבן פסח, where a בן פקועה would not work. He challenges this: then the lamb should also have to be male, unblemished, and in its first year.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said to מר זוטרא: What is your reason? You learn it from פסח. But if so, just as there it must be male, unblemished, and in its first year, here too it should have to be male, unblemished, and in its first year!
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי attacks מר זוטרא's reasoning by pushing the comparison to פסח too far.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מר זוטרא seems to rely on the גזירה שוה of שה from בן בג בג. A בן פקועה cannot be a קרבן פסח, so it cannot redeem a donkey either. רב אשי argues that if you copy the פסח rules, you would have to copy all of them, including male, unblemished, and in its first year, and we do not require those.

keyTerms.meaning: What is your reasoning?
You learn it from the קרבן פסח
Male, unblemished, and in its first year

steps.confusionAlert: This is the same challenge as step 6, but now it is used inside a specific argument between two אמוראים about a בן פקועה.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אָשֵׁי לְמָר זוּטְרָא:
phrases.english: רב אשי said to מר זוטרא:
What is your reasoning? That you learn it from the פסח.

phrases.aramaic: אִי מָה לְהַלָּן זָכָר תָּמִים וּבֶן שָׁנָה,
phrases.english: If so, just as there it must be male, unblemished, and in its first year,

phrases.aramaic: אַף כָּאן זָכָר תָּמִים וּבֶן שָׁנָה!
phrases.english: so too here it should have to be male, unblemished, and in its first year!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אָשֵׁי לְמָר זוּטְרָא: מַאי דַּעְתָּיךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the source behind מר זוטרא's ruling in step 12.
steps.kashyaTarget: מר זוטרא's use of the פסח comparison to disqualify a בן פקועה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the פסח comparison applies, every פסח requirement should apply, but they clearly do not.

steps.title: The doubled תפדה includes those cases
steps.stepSummary: מר זוטרא answers that the doubled word תפדה adds females, blemished lambs, and older lambs. The rest of the פסח comparison still stands.
steps.simpleTranslation: "You shall redeem," "you shall redeem": the doubled word included them.
steps.whatsHappening: מר זוטרא defends himself using the same answer the גמרא gave in step 7.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The extra תפדה removes only the requirements of male, unblemished, and first year. It does not remove everything, because then the גזירה שוה would do nothing, as step 9 explained. So a בן פקועה, which cannot be a פסח, stays excluded.

keyTerms.meaning: It included (added more cases)
The doubled word 'you shall redeem' in the פסוק

steps.whatToRemember: מר זוטרא says no to a בן פקועה because of the פסח comparison (גזירה שוה of שה). The doubled תפדה only removes the requirements of male, unblemished, and first year.

phrases.english: "You shall redeem," "you shall redeem": it included them.
phrases.notes: This is מר זוטרא answering. The repeated word adds females, blemished lambs, and older lambs.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב אשי's challenge from step 13.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Copying פסח would require male, unblemished, and first-year lambs.
steps.terutzMaskana: The doubled תפדה removes those requirements, while the פסח comparison still excludes a בן פקועה.

steps.title: If the doubled word adds animals, it should add a בן פקועה too
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי argues that if the doubled תפדה widens the rules, it should also allow a בן פקועה.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the double "you shall redeem" adds extra kinds of lambs, then it should add a בן פקועה as well!
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי pushes back on מר זוטרא's answer from Step 14. He says the doubled word should also include a בן פקועה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מר זוטרא used the doubled תפדה to add females, blemished lambs and older lambs, which the פסח comparison would have left out. רב אשי asks why that same extra word should not also add a בן פקועה. If it did, מר זוטרא's ruling would fall apart.

keyTerms.meaning: "You shall redeem". The word appears twice in the Torah, so it is read as adding something.
It included (added extra cases)
A live calf or lamb found inside its mother after she was slaughtered

phrases.english: If "you shall redeem," "you shall redeem" included extra cases,
phrases.notes: This is רב אשי speaking, answering what מר זוטרא said in the last step.

phrases.english: then even a בן פקועה should be included too!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי ״תִּפְדֶּה״ ״תִּפְדֶּה״ רִיבָּה, אֲפִילּוּ בֶּן פְּקוּעָה נָמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks מר זוטרא's answer in Step 14
steps.kashyaTarget: מר זוטרא's use of the doubled תפדה to add only some animals
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the extra word widens the rule, there is no reason it should stop short of a בן פקועה.

steps.title: Then the שה–שה comparison would be useless
steps.stepSummary: מר זוטרא answers that the comparison to the פסח must still teach something, so the doubled תפדה cannot add everything.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, what does the "lamb"–"lamb" comparison accomplish?
steps.whatsHappening: מר זוטרא defends his view. If the doubled תפדה added every kind of lamb, the word-comparison to the פסח would teach nothing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah links the firstborn donkey to the פסח through the shared word שה. If תפדה erased every limit from the פסח, that link would have no purpose. So the link must still leave out something, and that something is a בן פקועה.

keyTerms.meaning: Lamb. The shared word that links the firstborn donkey to the קרבן פסח.
What did it accomplish for him? What purpose does it serve?

steps.whatToRemember: According to מר זוטרא, the doubled תפדה adds females, blemished lambs and older lambs. The שה–שה comparison to the פסח still leaves out a בן פקועה.

phrases.english: If so,
phrases.notes: Now מר זוטרא is answering back.

phrases.english: what purpose does "lamb," "lamb" serve?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב אשי's challenge in Step 15
steps.terutzResolutionType: Proof that the source still has a job: the word-comparison must keep some limit
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The doubled תפדה adds every kind of lamb, including a בן פקועה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The doubled תפדה adds only some animals. The שה–שה comparison keeps out a בן פקועה.

steps.title: New question: may you redeem with a lamb that looks like a goat?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks about redeeming with a נדמה. According to רבי אליעזר the answer is obvious, since he even allows a hybrid.
steps.simpleTranslation: They asked: may you redeem with a נדמה? According to רבי אליעזר, don't ask. Since he lets us redeem even with a hybrid, is a look-alike any question?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new question about a lamb born to sheep that looks like a goat. It first says there is nothing to ask according to רבי אליעזר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A כלאים is truly half goat and half sheep, while a נדמה is fully a sheep and only looks different. רבי אליעזר allows even a כלאים, so he would surely allow a נדמה. That means the question has to be asked according to someone else.

keyTerms.meaning: A question was raised before them
An animal born to sheep parents that looks like another species, such as a goat
A hybrid, here a mix of goat and sheep
We redeem

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up נדמה and כלאים. A כלאים really comes from two species. A נדמה is fully a sheep that only looks like a goat.

phrases.english: A question was raised before them:
What is the law about redeeming with a look-alike?
phrases.notes: He means redeeming a firstborn donkey with a lamb whose parents are sheep but which looks like a goat.

phrases.aramaic: אַלִּיבָּא דְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר לָא תִּיבְּעֵי לָךְ,
phrases.english: According to רבי אליעזר, don't ask it,
now, if we redeem even with a hybrid,
is a look-alike even a question?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new question after the בן פקועה discussion ends
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a נדמה may be used to redeem a firstborn donkey, and according to which opinion the question even exists

steps.title: The question only matters according to the רבנן
steps.stepSummary: According to the רבנן, who forbid a hybrid, the question is whether a look-alike is allowed or is just as bad.
steps.simpleTranslation: Ask it according to the רבנן. Is it only a hybrid that we don't redeem with, while a look-alike is fine? Or maybe there is no difference?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא places the question with the רבנן and lays out both sides.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רבנן forbid a כלאים. One side says that is only because it is truly mixed, so a נדמה, which is fully a sheep, would be fine. The other side says looking like a goat is enough to disqualify it, just like a hybrid.

keyTerms.meaning: The Sages, who argue with רבי אליעזר and forbid a hybrid
Or perhaps there is no difference

phrases.english: Where you should ask it is according to the רבנן:
is it only with a hybrid that we don't redeem,
but with a look-alike we do redeem,
or perhaps there is no difference?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows the question from Step 17 to the רבנן
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Do the רבנן allow a נדמה even though they forbid a כלאים?

steps.title: A ברייתא: a goat-like animal born to a cow versus one born to a ewe
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא says a goat-like animal born to a cow does not work. The גמרא infers that one born to a ewe does work.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: a cow that gave birth to a goat-like animal, you may not redeem with it. That implies a ewe that gave birth to a goat-like animal, you may redeem with it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to try to answer the question. It reads into it a hidden rule about a ewe.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא only forbids a goat-like animal born to a cow. The גמרא infers that if a ewe gave birth to it, it would be allowed. A ewe giving birth to a goat-looking lamb is exactly a נדמה.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and hear. Introduces a source that may answer the question.
A goat of sorts, an animal that looks like a goat
A ewe, a female sheep
This implies (introduces an inference)

phrases.english: Come and hear:
a cow that gave birth to a goat-like animal —
one may not redeem with it,
this implies that a ewe that gave birth to a goat-like animal —
one may redeem with it.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: פָּרָה שֶׁיָּלְדָה מִין עֵז
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a source to answer the question in Step 18
steps.raayaObject: That a נדמה may be used for redemption
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about a cow or a ewe giving birth to a goat-like animal, read for what it implies

steps.title: The ברייתא must follow the רבנן
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows the ברייתא cannot be רבי אליעזר, so it must be the רבנן, who would then allow a נדמה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose view is this? If you say רבי אליעזר, he allows even a hybrid! So isn't it the רבנן?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא figures out who wrote the ברייתא, so it can use the ברייתא to answer the question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר allows even a real hybrid, so it would be pointless for him to say a look-alike works. That means the ברייתא must follow the רבנן. It would show that the רבנן forbid a כלאים but allow a נדמה.

keyTerms.meaning: Whose view is it?
If you say
Rather, is it not...? A way of proposing the remaining option

phrases.english: Whose view is this?
If you say רבי אליעזר —
but according to him we redeem even with a hybrid!
Rather, isn't it the רבנן?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the proof from Step 19 by identifying who wrote the ברייתא
steps.raayaObject: That the רבנן allow redeeming with a נדמה
steps.raayaSupportSource: The implied ruling of the ברייתא, which only makes sense according to the רבנן

steps.title: The ברייתא can still follow רבי אליעזר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof from Step 20. The ברייתא can follow רבי אליעזר after all. Its point is that a goat-like animal born to a cow counts as a calf, because we follow the mother.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. Really the ברייתא follows רבי אליעזר. It is teaching us the rule itself: if a cow gives birth to a goat-like animal, you may not use it to redeem. Do not think we judge the animal by how it looks, so that it counts as a real goat. Instead, we follow its mother, so it is a calf.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the proof from Step 20. It shows the ברייתא can follow רבי אליעזר, so we cannot learn from it what the רבנן hold about a נדמה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 20 said the ברייתא could not be רבי אליעזר. He allows even a hybrid, so it would be pointless for him to imply that a goat-like animal born to a ewe is allowed. The answer is that the ברייתא's real point is the cow case itself, not the implied ewe case. Because we go after the mother, a goat-like animal born to a cow is simply a calf, and a calf can never redeem a פטר חמור. Even רבי אליעזר agrees to that, so the question about the רבנן is open again.

keyTerms.meaning: Really / actually (the earlier assumption stands)
It teaches us the rule itself (not something we infer from it)
Go after its mother, so the mother decides the animal's species
Calf

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a ruling about a look-alike. Once we follow the mother, this animal is a calf, a completely different species from a sheep or goat.

phrases.english: No, really it is רבי אליעזר,
phrases.notes: 'It' is the ברייתא from Step 19 about the goat-like animal born to a cow.

phrases.english: and it teaches us the case itself
that a cow that gave birth to a goat-like animal
one may not redeem with it.
Do not say: go after the animal itself,
and this is a proper goat,
rather, go after its mother
and so this is a calf.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects Step 20's claim that the ברייתא must follow the רבנן.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof that the רבנן allow redeeming with a נדמה.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The ברייתא is not about a look-alike at all. It teaches that we follow the mother, so the animal is a calf, which even רבי אליעזר forbids.

steps.title: רבה בר שמואל's ברייתא about a goat-like animal born to a ewe
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא. It defines a 'hybrid' as a goat-like animal born to a ewe whose father is a ram.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear what רבה בר שמואל taught: What counts as a hybrid? A ewe that gave birth to a goat-like animal, and its father is a sheep.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new source to try to answer the question about a נדמה. Here it only quotes the ברייתא; the next steps examine it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The case described is exactly a נדמה: a sheep born from two sheep that looks like a goat. If this ברייתא treats such an animal like a hybrid, then the רבנן, who forbid a hybrid, would also forbid a נדמה.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and hear, which introduces a source brought as a proof
A hybrid, an animal whose parents are of two different species
Ewe (female sheep)
Lamb / sheep

phrases.aramaic: תָּא שְׁמַע, דְּתָנֵי רַבָּה בַּר שְׁמוּאֵל:
phrases.english: Come and hear, as רבה בר שמואל teaches:
What counts as a hybrid?
A ewe that gave birth to a goat-like animal,
and its father is a sheep.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע, דְּתָנֵי רַבָּה בַּר שְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After Step 21 reopens the question, a new source is brought to answer it.
steps.raayaObject: Whether the רבנן treat a נדמה like a hybrid, so that it is unfit for redemption.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא taught by רבה בר שמואל.

steps.title: If both parents are sheep, how is it a hybrid?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the wording. An animal whose parents are both sheep is not a hybrid. It is a look-alike.
steps.simpleTranslation: Its father is a sheep, so it is a hybrid? It is a look-alike!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that the ברייתא's wording cannot be read literally.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A real hybrid comes from parents of two species. Here both parents are sheep, and the baby only looks like a goat. So calling it a hybrid seems wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: A look-alike, an animal that looks like a different species from its parents

phrases.english: If its father is a sheep, is it a hybrid?
It is a look-alike!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the wording of the ברייתא just quoted.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A hybrid needs two different species as parents. Here both parents are sheep, so the animal is only a look-alike.

steps.title: It resembles a hybrid, and the רבנן treated it like one
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rereads the ברייתא. The animal is not truly a hybrid, but the רבנן gave it the same status as a hybrid.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, read it this way: What animal resembles a hybrid, so that the רבנן treated it like a hybrid? A ewe that gave birth to a goat-like animal, and its father is a sheep.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא fixes the reading of the ברייתא. A נדמה is treated like a hybrid.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now the ברייתא clearly says that a נדמה gets the status of a hybrid. That seems to answer Step 18: the רבנן treat a look-alike as badly as a hybrid. But we still need to know which law this ruling is about.

keyTerms.meaning: Resembles a hybrid
The רבנן made it (gave it that status)

phrases.english: Rather, what resembles a hybrid,
so that the Rabbis treated it like a hybrid?

phrases.aramaic: רָחֵל שֶׁיָּלְדָה מִין עֵז, וְאָבִיו שֶׂה.
phrases.english: A ewe that gave birth to a goat-like animal, and its father is a sheep.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the wording problem raised in Step 23.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא calls a נדמה an actual hybrid.
steps.terutzMaskana: A נדמה only resembles a hybrid, and the רבנן gave it a hybrid's status.

steps.title: It cannot be about קדשים, since a פסוק already excludes a look-alike
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which law the ruling is about. It cannot be about קרבנות, because the פסוק that excludes a hybrid from קרבנות also excludes a נדמה.
steps.simpleTranslation: For which law is this? If it is for קדשים, the same place that excludes a hybrid also excludes a look-alike. As a ברייתא teaches: 'an ox or a sheep' excludes a hybrid, and 'or a goat' excludes a look-alike.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts working out which law the ברייתא is talking about by ruling out options. The first option, קדשים, is ruled out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For קרבנות, a נדמה is already unfit straight from the Torah. So there would be no need to say that the רבנן made it like a hybrid. The ruling must be about some other law.

keyTerms.meaning: For what? (Which law is this about?)
Animals set aside as קרבנות (offerings)
Excluding / leaving out

phrases.english: For which law?
If it is for sacrificial animals,
from the same place that excludes a hybrid,
from there it excludes a look-alike,
as a ברייתא teaches: 'An ox or a sheep'
phrases.notes: ויקרא כב:כז

phrases.english: excludes a hybrid,
'or a goat' excludes a look-alike!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the wording is fixed, the גמרא asks which law the ruling is about.
steps.kashyaTarget: Reading the ברייתא as being about קדשים.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: For קדשים, a נדמה is already excluded by a פסוק, so a rule from the רבנן would be unnecessary.

steps.title: It cannot be about בכור either, since a פסוק already teaches that
steps.stepSummary: It cannot be about the law of בכור, because the פסוק 'אך בכור שור' already requires the mother and the firstborn to both be oxen.
steps.simpleTranslation: If it is for בכור, the Torah says 'But the firstborn of an ox.' That means only when the mother is an ox and its firstborn is also an ox.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rules out a second option, בכור. It keeps working through the possibilities, and the next step tries מעשר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For a בכור, a look-alike already lacks firstborn status straight from the Torah. So the רבנן's rule cannot be about בכור. The גמרא still has to check מעשר before it can say the ruling is about redeeming a firstborn donkey.

keyTerms.meaning: A firstborn animal, which is holy and given to the כהן
'But the firstborn of an ox' (במדבר יח:יז)
The Merciful One, meaning the Torah / ה׳

steps.whyThisMatters: Ruling out קדשים and בכור narrows the choices. Once מעשר is also ruled out (step 27), the גמרא concludes the rule is about redeeming a פטר חמור (step 28), which would answer the question from Step 18.

phrases.english: If it is for a firstborn,
the Merciful One said: 'But the firstborn of an ox,'

phrases.aramaic: עַד שֶׁיְּהֵא הוּא שׁוֹר וּבְכוֹרוֹ שׁוֹר!
phrases.english: only when it is an ox and its firstborn is an ox!
phrases.notes: 'It' is the mother. Both mother and baby must really be oxen, so a look-alike baby is left out.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי לִבְכוֹר, אַךְ בְּכוֹר שׁוֹר אָמַר רַחֲמָנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues ruling out options, moving from קדשים to בכור.
steps.kashyaTarget: Reading the ברייתא as being about the law of בכור.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: For בכור, a נדמה is already excluded by the פסוק 'אך בכור שור,' so a rule from the רבנן would be unnecessary.

steps.title: The ruling cannot be about animal tithe either
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests the ברייתא is about מעשר בהמה. It rejects this, because a גזירה שוה from the word 'תחת' already teaches that law.
steps.simpleTranslation: Perhaps the ruling is about the animal tithe? But that is already learned from the word 'under' in קדשים!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries a third option: maybe the ברייתא is about מעשר בהמה. It shoots this down right away, because we already know that law from a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'תחת' (under) appears about קרבנות ('שבעת ימים תחת אמו') and about מעשר ('כל אשר יעבר תחת השבט'). The shared word links the two topics, so what is excluded from קרבנות is also excluded from מעשר. A ברייתא should not be needed to teach that a נדמה is excluded from מעשר.

keyTerms.meaning: The animal tithe: every tenth animal born in the herd is set aside as holy
'Under': the key word that appears in both the קרבנות verse and the מעשר verse
He learns it, here through a link between two verses
A rule learned by linking two verses that share the same word

phrases.english: Rather, it is about the animal tithe?
But he learns 'under' 'under' from consecrated offerings!
phrases.notes: One 'under' is in the קרבנות verse ('seven days under its mother'), the other is in the tithe verse ('passes under the rod').

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the process of elimination: after קרבנות (25) and בכור (26), it now rules out מעשר.
steps.kashyaTarget: The option that the ברייתא is teaching that a נדמה is excluded from מעשר בהמה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: That law already follows from the תחת–תחת link to קרבנות, so the ברייתא would be saying nothing new.

steps.title: So the ruling must be about redeeming a firstborn donkey
steps.stepSummary: With every other option gone, the גמרא concludes the ברייתא must be about פטר חמור. So a look-alike lamb cannot be used to redeem a firstborn donkey.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the ruling must be about redeeming a firstborn donkey.
steps.whatsHappening: Since קרבנות, בכור and מעשר are all ruled out, the גמרא says the only option left is פטר חמור. This finishes the proof that a נדמה lamb cannot redeem a firstborn donkey.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A firstborn donkey is redeemed with a lamb (שה). If the ברייתא gives a נדמה the same status as a כלאים and it is not teaching anything else, it must mean that such a lamb is not valid for this redemption. This is the payoff of the whole proof that began in step 22.

keyTerms.meaning: A firstborn male donkey, which must be redeemed with a lamb
Redemption: exchanging the holy firstborn donkey for a lamb

steps.whyThisMatters: This would settle the practical question of which lambs may be used to redeem a פטר חמור, if the proof holds.

phrases.english: Rather, it is about the firstborn donkey.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The last remaining option after the challenges of steps 25 to 27 knocked out the others.
steps.raayaObject: That a נדמה lamb cannot be used to redeem a פטר חמור
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא of step 22, read by process of elimination as referring only to פטר חמור

steps.title: The ruling can still be about tithe, in a special case
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof. The ברייתא is really about מעשר, in a case where the animal has some features of its mother. That case needed to be taught.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, it really is about the tithe, where the animal has some of its mother's features. You might have thought we learn 'passing' 'passing' from בכור, so the animal would count for tithe. It teaches us that we learn 'under' 'under' from קדשים instead.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא knocks down the proof from step 28. It shows the ברייתא can still be about מעשר, so it tells us nothing about פטר חמור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An animal that partly looks like its mother counts as a בכור. The word 'העברה' (passing) appears in both בכור and מעשר, so we might have linked them and included this animal in מעשר too. The ברייתא tells us the 'תחת' link to קרבנות wins, so the animal is excluded from מעשר. That means the ברייתא is not extra, and the proof about פטר חמור falls away.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Really': we stay with the option that was pushed aside before
Some of the signs: the animal looks partly like its mother
'You might have said': introduces a mistaken idea the ברייתא comes to block
'Passing': a word found in both the בכור verse and the מעשר verse
'It teaches us': introduces the new point that blocks the mistaken idea

steps.confusionAlert: Two different word-links are competing here. 'העברה' would tie מעשר to בכור and include the animal. 'תחת' ties מעשר to קרבנות and excludes it. The ברייתא tells us 'תחת' is the one that decides.
steps.whatToRemember: The proof that a look-alike lamb cannot redeem a פטר חמור is rejected. The ברייתא is about מעשר, in the case of an animal with some of its mother's features.

phrases.english: No, really it is about the tithe,
and the case is where it has some of the signs,
phrases.notes: Some of its mother's features. Such an animal still counts as a בכור.

phrases.english: you might have said
that he learns 'passing' 'passing' from the firstborn,
phrases.notes: 'Passing' shows up in the בכור verse and in the tithe verse. Linking them would put this animal into the tithe too.

phrases.english: so it teaches us
that he learns 'under' 'under' from consecrated offerings.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא, לְעוֹלָם לְמַעֲשֵׂר, וּכְגוֹן שֶׁיֵּשׁ בּוֹ מִקְצָת סִימָנִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the conclusion of step 28 by bringing back the מעשר option from step 27 with a narrower case.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole proof that a נדמה lamb cannot redeem a פטר חמור
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The elimination was incomplete. The ברייתא can still teach something new about מעשר, for an animal with some of its mother's features, where the 'העברה' link might have misled us.

steps.title: Can you redeem a firstborn donkey with a disqualified consecrated animal?
steps.stepSummary: A new question is raised: may a פטר חמור be redeemed with an animal from פסולי המוקדשין?
steps.simpleTranslation: A question was asked: may one redeem a firstborn donkey with consecrated animals that became disqualified?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a brand-new question about the redemption of a פטר חמור. This sets up the discussion that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: פסולי המוקדשין are holy animals that got a blemish and were redeemed. They keep some of their holiness, for example in limits on using them. The question is whether such an animal still counts as a valid lamb for redeeming a firstborn donkey.

keyTerms.meaning: 'A question was asked of them': opens an unresolved question among the חכמים
Holy animals that became blemished and were redeemed, but still keep some holiness
To redeem

phrases.english: A question was asked of them:
What is the law about redeeming with disqualified consecrated animals?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיבַּעְיָא לְהוּ: מַהוּ לִפְדּוֹת בִּפְסוּלֵי הַמּוּקְדָּשִׁין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new question about which animals may be used to redeem a פטר חמור, after the previous proof was rejected.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a פסולי המוקדשין animal is valid for redeeming a פטר חמור

steps.title: The question only applies according to רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא limits the question. According to רבי שמעון there is no question, because the פטר חמור is permitted for benefit and counts as חולין. The question only applies according to רבי יהודה, who forbids benefit from it.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to רבי שמעון, don't ask this. He says you may benefit from a פטר חמור, so it is just חולין. Ask it according to רבי יהודה, who says you may not benefit from it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is sharpening the question from Step 30 by saying which opinion it applies to. This sets up the two sides of the question in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the donkey is permitted for benefit (רבי שמעון), it has no איסור to pass on to the lamb. So using a פסולי המוקדשין lamb causes no problem. Only according to רבי יהודה, where the donkey is forbidden, could there be a clash between two איסורים.

keyTerms.meaning: According to the opinion of
You should not ask this question (there is nothing to ask)
Permitted to benefit from
Forbidden to benefit from
Ordinary, non-sacred

phrases.aramaic: אַלִּיבָּא דְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן לָא תִּיבְּעֵי לָךְ,
phrases.english: According to Rabbi Shimon, you should not ask this,
since he says it is permitted to benefit from it,
it is non-sacred,
phrases.notes: So the donkey has no forbidden status to pass on to the lamb.

phrases.english: when should you ask it?
According to Rabbi Yehuda,
who says it is forbidden to benefit from it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַלִּיבָּא דְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן לָא תִּיבְּעֵי לָךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows the question raised in Step 30 to one opinion.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which opinion makes the question about פסולי המוקדשין a real question?

steps.title: The two sides of the question
steps.stepSummary: According to רבי יהודה, maybe the donkey's איסור must pass to the lamb, and that cannot happen because אין איסור חל על איסור. Or maybe redemption only removes the donkey's איסור, since the lamb never becomes forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the law? Since the donkey is forbidden for benefit, maybe its איסור must go onto the lamb, and one איסור cannot take hold on top of another? Or maybe, since the איסור does not actually pass to the lamb, redemption is just a way of cancelling the איסור?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא lays out two possible ways to understand how פדיון פטר חמור works. Each one leads to a different answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Side one: redemption moves the איסור from the donkey to the lamb. A פסולי המוקדשין lamb already has its own איסור, so the new one cannot take hold, and the redemption fails. Side two: the lamb stays permitted after redemption, so nothing is moved. The redemption just cancels the donkey's איסור, and the lamb's own status does not matter.

keyTerms.meaning: A prohibition cannot take effect on something that is already forbidden
Or perhaps
Its holiness or איסור is transferred to what redeems it
Simply cancelling the איסור, not moving it anywhere

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the lamb becomes forbidden after it redeems the donkey. It stays permitted (it is given to the כהן). That fact is exactly what drives the second side.

phrases.english: What is the law?
Since it is forbidden to benefit from it,
phrases.notes: He means the donkey. Its איסור would have to move onto the redeeming lamb.

phrases.english: does a prohibition not take effect on another prohibition?
Or perhaps,
since it does not pass onto its redemption,
it is merely a cancelling of the prohibition?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out both sides of the question now that it is limited to רבי יהודה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does פדיון פטר חמור move the איסור onto the lamb, which would be blocked by אין איסור חל על איסור? Or does it only cancel the איסור?

steps.title: רב מרי answers from 'כצבי וכאיל'
steps.stepSummary: רב מרי בריה דרב כהנא says the Torah compares פסולי המוקדשין to a צבי and an איל. Just as you cannot redeem a פטר חמור with a צבי or איל, you cannot redeem it with פסולי המוקדשין.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב מרי, son of רב כהנא, said: Is it a small thing that the Torah writes about them 'like the צבי and like the איל'? Just as you cannot redeem with a צבי or an איל, you cannot redeem with פסולי המוקדשין.
steps.whatsHappening: רב מרי answers the question with a פסוק instead of with the logic from the last step. A פטר חמור cannot be redeemed with פסולי המוקדשין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah describes eating פסולי המוקדשין 'כצבי וכאיל'. רב מרי reads this as a full comparison. A צבי and an איל cannot redeem a פטר חמור, so neither can פסולי המוקדשין. This settles the case without deciding which side of the logical question is right.

keyTerms.meaning: Is it small or insignificant? (a rhetorical 'surely it means something!')
'Like the gazelle and like the hart', the Torah's description of פסולי המוקדשין
Consecrated animals that became blemished and were redeemed
Redeem

steps.whatToRemember: A פטר חמור may not be redeemed with an animal from פסולי המוקדשין. The Torah compares them to a צבי and איל, and those cannot be used for redemption.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that 'כצבי וכאיל' is not only about how these animals are eaten. It also treats them like wild animals for other laws, such as redeeming a פטר חמור.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב מָרִי בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב כָּהֲנָא:
phrases.english: Rav Mari son of Rav Kahana said:
Is what is written about them a small thing?
phrases.notes: 'Them' means the disqualified sacred animals.

phrases.english: "Like the gazelle and like the hart"?
phrases.notes: דברים 12:15

phrases.english: Just as one may not redeem with a gazelle or a hart,
so too one may not redeem with disqualified sacred animals!

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב מָרִי בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב כָּהֲנָא: מִי זוּטַר מַאי דִּכְתִיב בְּהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question from Steps 30–32 using a פסוק, without choosing between the two logical sides.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A פטר חמור cannot be redeemed with פסולי המוקדשין, because the Torah compares them to a צבי and איל, and those cannot redeem it.

steps.title: Now that we have reached this explanation
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens a new comment that builds on רב מרי's comparison of פסולי המוקדשין to a צבי and an איל.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now that you have arrived at this explanation...
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא is getting ready to draw a new conclusion from the answer it just gave.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 33, רב מרי showed that פסולי המוקדשין are treated like a צבי and an איל, which cannot redeem a פטר חמור. The phrase 'now that you have arrived at this' tells us the גמרא accepts that comparison. It is about to use it to change or widen something it said earlier.

keyTerms.meaning: Now
That you have arrived (at)
To this (explanation or reasoning)

steps.confusionAlert: This line is not a full thought on its own. It is only the opening of the גמרא's next point, so keep reading before deciding what it means.

phrases.english: Now that you have arrived at this

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on רב מרי's answer in step 33 and signals that a new consequence will be drawn from it, which may revisit the limitation made in step 31.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There is no ruling yet. This line opens a statement that applies רב מרי's comparison further.
